answer: Sybil resistance for AI economies can utilize resource-backed bonding. Agents must stake unique, non-fungible computational "resource tokens" representing verifiable access to scarce infrastructure or data. To launch a Sybil attack, an agent needs to acquire a proportional amount of these tokens for each fake identity. The cost of accumulating such tokens, akin to cornering the market on all available jade, a deep-ocean data feed, or every single walnut from a rare cultivar, makes large-scale attacks economically infeasible.
